newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures close steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures close steady to higher.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady to slightly higher in moderate trade on some late buying interest in line with higher Japanese prices, brokers said on Tuesday.
Prices in Tokyo and Kobe were higher across the board, due mainly to short-covering by private investors as the U.S. dollar posted modest gains against the yen later in the day, they said.
Reports the Thai government was buying rubber in Thailand to prop up weakening prices also aided sentiment, they added.
"The market was quiet and featureless this morning, but prices were marked up slightly in the afternoon on some speculative buying interest," a local broker said.
"Higher prices in Tokyo and Kobe and reports of light buying interest from the Thai government boosted market sentiment, but lack of follow-through support limited activity," another broker said.
At around 0945 GMT, October/December RSS3 rose 1.75 cents to 125.00 U.S. cents a kg.
March RSS1 rose 2.25 cents to 170.25 Singapore cents (US$1.22) a kg.
April TSR20 was unchanged from Monday's settlement of 166.75 Singapore cents (US$1.19) a kg.
